name: Sorbonne Université
header:
Sorbonne Université
France · M1 Mathématiques et applications (general track); M2 Mathématiques fondamentales (Paris Centre joint teaching); PhD
via ED 386 after M2/equivalence
Relevant European programme; no numerical ranking asserted
Eligibility and preparation · Deadlines by stage · English and GRE · Academic records · Recommendation letters · Written
materials · Funding and fees · Conflicts and remaining checks · Faculty · Sources
Pay attention to
• The likely US-resident non-EU academic deadline precedes PGSM: 15 January 2027 at 6 pm EST versus 22
January 2027 at 23:59 Paris.
• A four-year BA is not automatically French M1 equivalence. A master’s/equivalent is normally needed before
PhD.
• Do not assume every Paris Centre course or researcher belongs to the same university.
• Sorbonne mathematics pages warn that outgoing mail to Gmail/Hotmail/Outlook/Live/Me domains is blocked
after a cyberattack; use your UChicago address and verify current delivery.
• Some faculty publication pages retain old lists; these entries identify the latest dated official evidence found,
not a claim that no newer work exists.
• Elba Garcia-Failde remains on the Sorbonne directory but her official-linked homepage places her at UPC
Barcelona, on leave since July 2025. Julien Marché is attached to ENS; see that dossier. These are not
unqualified on-campus Sorbonne supervisor suggestions.

sections.title: Eligibility and preparation
sections.text:
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
M1 is the usual bachelor’s-to-master’s route: a mathematics degree and adequate preparation are assessed. A
four-year UChicago BA does not automatically count as French M1; direct M2 requires individual M1
equivalence. ED 386 normally requires a research master’s/equivalent, an HDR-qualified supervisor, an agreed
project and institutional funding; personal self-funding is excluded. F-1 status establishes US residence/status,
not French admission or nationality eligibility. [s1] [s2] [s14]
Before submission [Standing rule]
For non-EU citizenship while resident in the US, the mathematics page directs applicants through Campus
France/Études en France. EU/EEA citizenship changes the route to MonMaster. Check the exact programme’s
portal listing and any additional institutional procedure. PGSM is an independent scholarship application;
choose one to three eligible master’s routes and also apply for admission. A Campus France review and
interview follow initial submission. [s1] [s4] [s5] [s9]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
For M1/M2, use programme coordinators to assess level equivalence and course preparation; an agreed thesis
supervisor is not a published master’s prerequisite. For PhD, an HDR supervisor in an ED 386 partner
laboratory and agreed research project are prerequisites. IMJ-PRG spans Sorbonne, Paris Cité and CNRS:
affiliation alone does not mean everyone is a Sorbonne professor. [s14] [s20]
Portal workflow [Standing rule]
eCandidat: activate account within five days, upload/merge supporting records and submit explicitly; statuses
distinguish received from complete. A displayed return deadline blocks later uploads. PGSM sends a
confirmation email and supports returning to complete the dossier. Keep scholarship and academic
applications separate. [s12] [s9]

Cycle verification [2027 confirmed]
2027 HDAP and PGSM deadlines are explicit. Sorbonne direct-platform calendars, doctoral competition and
fees still describe 2026 entry/2026-27; they are historical comparators. [s4] [s7] [s11] [s15] [s16]

sections.title: Deadlines by stage
sections.text:
Academic application [2027 confirmed]
US Études en France HDAP for fall 2027: opened 1 October 2026; initial application due 15 January 2027, 6 pm
EST. University responses by 30 April 2027. For an applicant routed to MonMaster/eCandidat instead, exact
2027 dates were not established. Prior 2026: M1 17 February-16 March; M2 26 March-11 June, some extensions
to 26 June. [s4] [s11]
Funding consideration [2027 confirmed]
PGSM fall 2027: 22 January 2027, 23:59 Paris time. ED 386 doctoral contracts: 2027 call not found; prior
application window 4 May-1 June 2026, committee 23 June. These PhD dates are not relevant until
master’s/equivalence and supervisor conditions are met. [s7] [s15]
Reference receipt [Unresolved]
PGSM standing FAQ permits referees two extra days after the applicant deadline; an explicitly dated 2027
reference cutoff/time was not found. Obtain confirmation rather than treating the scholarship deadline as the
letter deadline. Admission letters: no separate 2027 master’s reference deadline found. The prior ED 386
dossier, including optional support letters, was due 1 June 2026. [s10] [s15]
Test-score receipt [Unresolved]
For Études en France, upload French-test registration by the initial deadline if results are pending. Campus
France advises testing by December so results can be incorporated before final institutional transmission by
mid-March; no precise Sorbonne 2027 test-result day is published in checked pages. [s5]
Supporting documents [Standing rule]
HDAP initial dossier uses the application deadline. The advisor can request corrections before final
transmission. Where eCandidat applies, its displayed return deadline prevents later uploads/submission; no
general grace period is promised. PGSM requires a complete dossier, with the separate reference allowance
noted above. [s5] [s12] [s9]
Accepting an offer [2027 confirmed]
Études en France fall 2027: accept one offer by 31 May 2027. eCandidat applicants must use the confirmation
date shown in their individual offer. No uniform PGSM award-acceptance deadline was found. [s4] [s12]

sections.title: English and GRE
sections.text:
English requirement [Unresolved]
No TOEFL/IELTS requirement was established for the general French-taught M1/M2 route. French is the
relevant language: Science faculty recommends B2; the exact mandatory certificate/threshold for the selected
track must be checked in Études en France. Individual M2 courses may be English, but that does not prove the
whole degree is English-taught. [s13] [s20]
UChicago English exemption [Unresolved]
A UChicago English-medium degree does not establish a French-language exemption. Campus France exempts
applicants applying only to entirely English-taught programmes from French-test submission; confirm that the
chosen programme qualifies before relying on this. No specific UChicago English-test waiver was published. [s5]
GRE General; GRE Mathematics [Unresolved]

explicit prohibition on submitting a score; no formal GRE policy located. [s3] [s8] [s15]

sections.title: Academic records
sections.text:
Transcripts and degree records [Standing rule]
M2: four years of course records, grades and diplomas. Études en France: latest official transcript (unofficial
not accepted), most recent diploma; pending graduates add an institutional letter confirming
standing/expected graduation. French translations of academic documents must be professional for the
French-taught admissions route. PGSM requests bachelor’s and any master’s transcripts/diplomas; in-progress
students may provide all available higher-education grades. Doctoral contract: M1/M2 grades and M2 award
evidence if available. [s3] [s4] [s5] [s8] [s15] [s21]
Mathematics-course list [Standing rule]
M2 explicitly requires courses attended and passed over the preceding four years. Include the UChicago
sequence and graduate courses clearly; admission evaluates content, breadth and marks. [s2] [s3]
Course descriptions [Unresolved]
Course content is an M2 assessment criterion, but the public upload checklist specifies a course list rather than
a separately formatted syllabus document. Exact description length/template is not public. [s2] [s3]

sections.title: Recommendation letters
sections.text:
Number and type [Standing rule]
PGSM: one to three academic recommendations. Campus France generally suggests one or two, rather than
universally requiring them. The Sorbonne M2 public checklist does not specify a required count. ED 386 prior
contract call allows one or more optional support letters. [s4] [s8] [s15]
Scholarship references [Unresolved]
PGSM letters form a separate scholarship dossier. No published distinct referee questionnaire or requirement
for an additional referee beyond its one-to-three range was found. [s8] [s9]
What sends the invitation [Unresolved]
PGSM automatically emails professors through the application. The FAQ describes this as occurring when
completing/validating the application; it does not isolate whether simply saving an email before first validation
triggers a message. [s10]
Before versus after submission [Standing rule]
After first PGSM validation, the confirmation email contains a recommendation-upload link that can be
forwarded to additional professors or to a referee who did not receive the automatic message. Master’s
admission-platform trigger is not publicly established. [s10]
Receipt confirmation [Standing rule]
PGSM applicants can inspect their online dossier and see submitted letters but cannot read or delete the
letters. eCandidat shows document and dossier statuses, but this is not evidence of a confidential-referee
workflow. [s10] [s12]
Updating and reusing letters [Unresolved]
PGSM allows completion after initial validation and additional referee submissions through the confirmation
link. Applicants cannot delete letters; referee replacement/update or cross-year reuse policy is not stated.
eCandidat requires a new annual account. [s9] [s10] [s12]

sections.title: Written materials
sections.text:
Academic CV / resume [Standing rule]
Updated CV for Études en France and PGSM; no public page limit. Prior doctoral-contract CV must cover M1/M2
education and internships. [s4] [s8] [s15]

Statement of purpose [Standing rule]
Études en France motivation statement: at most 2,500 characters, in French for French-taught programmes or
English for English-taught programmes. Sorbonne M2 separately asks for a cover letter specifying proposed
courses; no length/format published. [s4] [s3]
Personal / background statement [Unresolved]
No separate personal/background essay listed in the checked public checklists. Do not infer that the live portal
has no short questions. [s3] [s8] [s15]
Research-interest statement [Standing rule]
PGSM motivation letter should explain mathematical preferences, professional plans and how the selected
master’s choices support them (paraphrase). No separate research-interest statement or public length limit
identified. [s9]
Research proposal [Prior cycle]
For a later ED 386 doctoral-contract application, the 2026 call required a one-to-three-page thesis project
identifying title and proposed supervisor. No PhD proposal is listed for the M1/M2 admissions route. [s15] [s3]
Writing sample / thesis / research summary [Unresolved]
No compulsory thesis, writing sample or research paper upload appears in the checked master’s/PGSM
checklists. A research internship and thesis are degree components after admission, not evidence of an
application writing-sample requirement. [s3] [s8] [s20]
Publications list [Unresolved]
No separate publication list or requirement to upload/link papers located. Relevant work can be identified in
the CV; that is a preparation suggestion, not a published requirement. [s3] [s8]
Course-list document [Standing rule]
Required for M2: list courses attended/passed during the previous four years, with corresponding grades. No
public page limit, template or file format. [s3]
Scholarship essays [Standing rule]
PGSM: CV, motivation letter, academic records and one-to-three letters; select one-to-three eligible master’s
programmes. Specific mathematical/career fit belongs in the motivation letter. No separate financial-need
essay or exact limit found. [s8] [s9]
Other short answers / materials [Prior cycle]
Prior ED 386 call: use its application form without altering formatting and include a motivation letter; dossier
sent by email to the two named administrators. For immigration/pre-consular processing after direct
admission, a separate short motivation text may again be required. [s15] [s19]

sections.title: Funding and fees
sections.text:
Amount and coverage [Standing rule]
PGSM published rate €1,150/month: M1 first year €13,800 over 12 months; M2 €12,650 over 11 months, or
€13,800 if the specified 12th-month condition applies (annual totals calculated). Registration and student
social coverage are included in published rules; international awardees receive a CROUS reservation and
annual economy home-country round trip. PhD public-contract minimum in 2026 is €2,300 gross/month
(€27,600 gross/year calculated); this is a statutory baseline, not a guaranteed 2027 offer. [s8] [s9] [s18]
Years of support [Standing rule]
PGSM M1: 12 months then 11/12 months subject to successful first-year exams; M2: 11 months plus one if
continuing to a French doctorate or internship lasts through August. Scholarship starts 1 September and
awardees should be present then. Doctoral contracts normally last three years. [s8] [s9] [s15]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
PGSM’s international call is intended for students studying outside France; UChicago study fits that location

condition. Nationality and any additional eligibility conditions still require the actual call review. French
doctoral employment is a separate competitive route; foreign doctoral scholarships are explicitly allowed by ED
386. [s8] [s14]
Conditions and duties [Standing rule]
Master’s admission does not guarantee funding, and PGSM selection does not constitute master’s enrollment.
Renewal requires successful studies. For ED 386, secure funding and supervisor before registration; a
self-financed thesis is not permitted by its published conditions. [s9] [s14]
Extra funding application [Standing rule]
Submit PGSM separately from university admission. Later doctoral-contract competition is another application;
optional doctoral teaching missions require their own portal application in the prior call. [s9] [s15]
Other funding routes [Unresolved]
ED 386 lists company-linked CIFRE employment and foreign doctoral scholarships as alternatives to a
university contract. Investigate project-funded positions with an HDR supervisor; no blanket master’s stipend
or TA guarantee was found. [s14]
Application fee [Standing rule]
Campus France USA full DAP/HDAP admissions processing: US$460; this is not the lower US$270 regular
pre-consular fee for already-admitted HDAP allégé applicants. No separate Sorbonne academic application fee
established. Prior 2026-27 national tuition: master’s €255/year, doctorate €398/year, plus CVEC where
applicable; 2027-28 amounts not established. [s6] [s16]
Fee waiver [Prior cycle]
Sorbonne’s July 2026 decision aims to reduce non-EU tuition to domestic levels for 2026-27; eligible new
entrants must request exemption through the student-aid portal. This policy is not a confirmed 2027-28 waiver.
Campus France application-fee waiver was not established. PGSM published terms cover university
registration. [s16] [s17] [s9]

Relevant European programme; no numerical ranking asserted

materials · Funding and fees · Conflicts and remaining checks · Faculty · Sources
Pay attention to
• The likely US-resident non-EU academic deadline precedes PGSM: 15 January 2027 at 6 pm EST versus 22
January 2027 at 23:59 Paris.
• A four-year BA is not automatically French M1 equivalence. A master’s/equivalent is normally needed before
PhD.
• Do not assume every Paris Centre course or researcher belongs to the same university.
• Sorbonne mathematics pages warn that outgoing mail to Gmail/Hotmail/Outlook/Live/Me domains is blocked
after a cyberattack; use your UChicago address and verify current delivery.
• Some faculty publication pages retain old lists; these entries identify the latest dated official evidence found,
not a claim that no newer work exists.
• Elba Garcia-Failde remains on the Sorbonne directory but her official-linked homepage places her at UPC
Barcelona, on leave since July 2025. Julien Marché is attached to ENS; see that dossier. These are not
unqualified on-campus Sorbonne supervisor suggestions.
Eligibility and preparation
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
M1 is the usual bachelor’s-to-master’s route: a mathematics degree and adequate preparation are assessed. A
four-year UChicago BA does not automatically count as French M1; direct M2 requires individual M1
equivalence. ED 386 normally requires a research master’s/equivalent, an HDR-qualified supervisor, an agreed
project and institutional funding; personal self-funding is excluded. F-1 status establishes US residence/status,
not French admission or nationality eligibility. [s1] [s2] [s14]
Before submission [Standing rule]
For non-EU citizenship while resident in the US, the mathematics page directs applicants through Campus
France/Études en France. EU/EEA citizenship changes the route to MonMaster. Check the exact programme’s
portal listing and any additional institutional procedure. PGSM is an independent scholarship application;
choose one to three eligible master’s routes and also apply for admission. A Campus France review and
interview follow initial submission. [s1] [s4] [s5] [s9]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
For M1/M2, use programme coordinators to assess level equivalence and course preparation; an agreed thesis
supervisor is not a published master’s prerequisite. For PhD, an HDR supervisor in an ED 386 partner
laboratory and agreed research project are prerequisites. IMJ-PRG spans Sorbonne, Paris Cité and CNRS:
affiliation alone does not mean everyone is a Sorbonne professor. [s14] [s20]
Portal workflow [Standing rule]
eCandidat: activate account within five days, upload/merge supporting records and submit explicitly; statuses
distinguish received from complete. A displayed return deadline blocks later uploads. PGSM sends a
confirmation email and supports returning to complete the dossier. Keep scholarship and academic
applications separate. [s12] [s9]

Cycle verification [2027 confirmed]
2027 HDAP and PGSM deadlines are explicit. Sorbonne direct-platform calendars, doctoral competition and
fees still describe 2026 entry/2026-27; they are historical comparators. [s4] [s7] [s11] [s15] [s16]
Deadlines by stage
Academic application [2027 confirmed]
US Études en France HDAP for fall 2027: opened 1 October 2026; initial application due 15 January 2027, 6 pm
EST. University responses by 30 April 2027. For an applicant routed to MonMaster/eCandidat instead, exact
2027 dates were not established. Prior 2026: M1 17 February-16 March; M2 26 March-11 June, some extensions
to 26 June. [s4] [s11]
Funding consideration [2027 confirmed]
PGSM fall 2027: 22 January 2027, 23:59 Paris time. ED 386 doctoral contracts: 2027 call not found; prior
application window 4 May-1 June 2026, committee 23 June. These PhD dates are not relevant until
master’s/equivalence and supervisor conditions are met. [s7] [s15]
Reference receipt [Unresolved]
PGSM standing FAQ permits referees two extra days after the applicant deadline; an explicitly dated 2027
reference cutoff/time was not found. Obtain confirmation rather than treating the scholarship deadline as the
letter deadline. Admission letters: no separate 2027 master’s reference deadline found. The prior ED 386
dossier, including optional support letters, was due 1 June 2026. [s10] [s15]
Test-score receipt [Unresolved]
For Études en France, upload French-test registration by the initial deadline if results are pending. Campus
France advises testing by December so results can be incorporated before final institutional transmission by
mid-March; no precise Sorbonne 2027 test-result day is published in checked pages. [s5]
Supporting documents [Standing rule]
HDAP initial dossier uses the application deadline. The advisor can request corrections before final
transmission. Where eCandidat applies, its displayed return deadline prevents later uploads/submission; no
general grace period is promised. PGSM requires a complete dossier, with the separate reference allowance
noted above. [s5] [s12] [s9]
Accepting an offer [2027 confirmed]
Études en France fall 2027: accept one offer by 31 May 2027. eCandidat applicants must use the confirmation
date shown in their individual offer. No uniform PGSM award-acceptance deadline was found. [s4] [s12]
English and GRE
English requirement [Unresolved]
No TOEFL/IELTS requirement was established for the general French-taught M1/M2 route. French is the
relevant language: Science faculty recommends B2; the exact mandatory certificate/threshold for the selected
track must be checked in Études en France. Individual M2 courses may be English, but that does not prove the
whole degree is English-taught. [s13] [s20]
UChicago English exemption [Unresolved]
A UChicago English-medium degree does not establish a French-language exemption. Campus France exempts
applicants applying only to entirely English-taught programmes from French-test submission; confirm that the
chosen programme qualifies before relying on this. No specific UChicago English-test waiver was published. [s5]
GRE General; GRE Mathematics [Unresolved]
Neither GRE is listed among the checked admission, PGSM or doctoral-contract documents. This is not an
explicit prohibition on submitting a score; no formal GRE policy located. [s3] [s8] [s15]

Academic records
Transcripts and degree records [Standing rule]
M2: four years of course records, grades and diplomas. Études en France: latest official transcript (unofficial
not accepted), most recent diploma; pending graduates add an institutional letter confirming
standing/expected graduation. French translations of academic documents must be professional for the
French-taught admissions route. PGSM requests bachelor’s and any master’s transcripts/diplomas; in-progress
students may provide all available higher-education grades. Doctoral contract: M1/M2 grades and M2 award
evidence if available. [s3] [s4] [s5] [s8] [s15] [s21]
Mathematics-course list [Standing rule]
M2 explicitly requires courses attended and passed over the preceding four years. Include the UChicago
sequence and graduate courses clearly; admission evaluates content, breadth and marks. [s2] [s3]
Course descriptions [Unresolved]
Course content is an M2 assessment criterion, but the public upload checklist specifies a course list rather than
a separately formatted syllabus document. Exact description length/template is not public. [s2] [s3]
Recommendation letters
Number and type [Standing rule]
PGSM: one to three academic recommendations. Campus France generally suggests one or two, rather than
universally requiring them. The Sorbonne M2 public checklist does not specify a required count. ED 386 prior
contract call allows one or more optional support letters. [s4] [s8] [s15]
Scholarship references [Unresolved]
PGSM letters form a separate scholarship dossier. No published distinct referee questionnaire or requirement
for an additional referee beyond its one-to-three range was found. [s8] [s9]
What sends the invitation [Unresolved]
PGSM automatically emails professors through the application. The FAQ describes this as occurring when
completing/validating the application; it does not isolate whether simply saving an email before first validation
triggers a message. [s10]
Before versus after submission [Standing rule]
After first PGSM validation, the confirmation email contains a recommendation-upload link that can be
forwarded to additional professors or to a referee who did not receive the automatic message. Master’s
admission-platform trigger is not publicly established. [s10]
Receipt confirmation [Standing rule]
PGSM applicants can inspect their online dossier and see submitted letters but cannot read or delete the
letters. eCandidat shows document and dossier statuses, but this is not evidence of a confidential-referee
workflow. [s10] [s12]
Updating and reusing letters [Unresolved]
PGSM allows completion after initial validation and additional referee submissions through the confirmation
link. Applicants cannot delete letters; referee replacement/update or cross-year reuse policy is not stated.
eCandidat requires a new annual account. [s9] [s10] [s12]

Academic CV / resume [Standing rule]
Updated CV for Études en France and PGSM; no public page limit. Prior doctoral-contract CV must cover M1/M2
education and internships. [s4] [s8] [s15]

Statement of purpose [Standing rule]
Études en France motivation statement: at most 2,500 characters, in French for French-taught programmes or
English for English-taught programmes. Sorbonne M2 separately asks for a cover letter specifying proposed
courses; no length/format published. [s4] [s3]
Personal / background statement [Unresolved]

has no short questions. [s3] [s8] [s15]

PGSM motivation letter should explain mathematical preferences, professional plans and how the selected
master’s choices support them (paraphrase). No separate research-interest statement or public length limit
identified. [s9]
Research proposal [Prior cycle]
For a later ED 386 doctoral-contract application, the 2026 call required a one-to-three-page thesis project
identifying title and proposed supervisor. No PhD proposal is listed for the M1/M2 admissions route. [s15] [s3]

No compulsory thesis, writing sample or research paper upload appears in the checked master’s/PGSM
checklists. A research internship and thesis are degree components after admission, not evidence of an
application writing-sample requirement. [s3] [s8] [s20]
Publications list [Unresolved]
No separate publication list or requirement to upload/link papers located. Relevant work can be identified in
the CV; that is a preparation suggestion, not a published requirement. [s3] [s8]
Course-list document [Standing rule]
Required for M2: list courses attended/passed during the previous four years, with corresponding grades. No
public page limit, template or file format. [s3]
Scholarship essays [Standing rule]
PGSM: CV, motivation letter, academic records and one-to-three letters; select one-to-three eligible master’s
programmes. Specific mathematical/career fit belongs in the motivation letter. No separate financial-need
essay or exact limit found. [s8] [s9]

sent by email to the two named administrators. For immigration/pre-consular processing after direct
admission, a separate short motivation text may again be required. [s15] [s19]
Funding and fees
Amount and coverage [Standing rule]
PGSM published rate €1,150/month: M1 first year €13,800 over 12 months; M2 €12,650 over 11 months, or
€13,800 if the specified 12th-month condition applies (annual totals calculated). Registration and student
social coverage are included in published rules; international awardees receive a CROUS reservation and
annual economy home-country round trip. PhD public-contract minimum in 2026 is €2,300 gross/month
(€27,600 gross/year calculated); this is a statutory baseline, not a guaranteed 2027 offer. [s8] [s9] [s18]
Years of support [Standing rule]
PGSM M1: 12 months then 11/12 months subject to successful first-year exams; M2: 11 months plus one if
continuing to a French doctorate or internship lasts through August. Scholarship starts 1 September and
awardees should be present then. Doctoral contracts normally last three years. [s8] [s9] [s15]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
PGSM’s international call is intended for students studying outside France; UChicago study fits that location

condition. Nationality and any additional eligibility conditions still require the actual call review. French
doctoral employment is a separate competitive route; foreign doctoral scholarships are explicitly allowed by ED
386. [s8] [s14]
Conditions and duties [Standing rule]
Master’s admission does not guarantee funding, and PGSM selection does not constitute master’s enrollment.
Renewal requires successful studies. For ED 386, secure funding and supervisor before registration; a
self-financed thesis is not permitted by its published conditions. [s9] [s14]
Extra funding application [Standing rule]
Submit PGSM separately from university admission. Later doctoral-contract competition is another application;
optional doctoral teaching missions require their own portal application in the prior call. [s9] [s15]
Other funding routes [Unresolved]
ED 386 lists company-linked CIFRE employment and foreign doctoral scholarships as alternatives to a
university contract. Investigate project-funded positions with an HDR supervisor; no blanket master’s stipend
or TA guarantee was found. [s14]

Campus France USA full DAP/HDAP admissions processing: US$460; this is not the lower US$270 regular

Sorbonne’s July 2026 decision aims to reduce non-EU tuition to domestic levels for 2026-27; eligible new
